about: The words of the memory-systems feed page. The page's data is its own noun, feeds-memory-systems.json, copied byte for byte from the feed's builder (functional/builds/memory-feed/agora), which reads it from the feed's records in Tessera. scripts/build_site.py renders both into site/feeds/memory-systems/index.html, says which Tessera the scans ran on, and shows the schedule only when the scans ran on hosted Tessera.
title: The memory-systems feed | Agora
description: A feed of new memory systems for agents: what appeared on GitHub in two days, which fits a given setup, and the benchmark claims each project makes, quoted from its own README or paper.
heading: The memory‑systems feed
lead: Hundreds of memory systems for agents appear on GitHub in days, far more than anyone can test. This feed gathers them, keeps each as a task object with its source, and answers which fits your setup from what it stored.
where_local: Scanned on a local copy of Tessera, with real reads of GitHub and arXiv
count_line: repositories created on GitHub in the 48 hours to
fits_lead: Each setup lists the best-fitting projects the feed stored: ranked by quoted evidence, then stars, then recent commits.
answer_label: The answer from stored task objects, with no model call
claims_lead: Numbers are the projects’ own claims, quoted from their README or paper and checked character by character. Nobody here re-ran them.
how: A timer enqueues one scan task within its allowance; a worker with a scoped key claims it and reads only official public APIs.
Each repository, paper and quoted claim becomes a task object with its source and the time it was seen, written with compare-and-set.
Extracting the benchmark claims and comparing the projects are follow-up tasks, each with its own receipt.
